post_title: Marvelous Design crashes on launch on Mac Pro
post_details: I've just installed Marvelous Designer 9 on my new Mac Pro (2019), and it crashes on launch every time after registering. This is version 5.1.477, and is registered with my existing Marvelous Designer 9 Personal Perpetual license. My Mac Pro is running macOS Monterey 12.4 (21F79). It has the AMD Radeon Pro W5700X 16 GB MPX module, with other GPUs connected as eGPUs. I couldn't immediately find a crash log to attach. Any help in getting up and running would be much appreciated. - Dave
post_description: This webpage aims to provide troubleshooting tips and solutions for users experiencing launch crashes with Marvelous Designer 9 on Mac Pro systems.

comments.comment_body: Hello 8322385113753, To your concern, please kindly note that Marvelous Designer is not fully supported with Monterey OS at the moment and the compatibility with it would be available within our next patch version, which is anticipated to be released in late Summer or early Fall this year. However, due to the different programming structure from version 9 and 10 of Marvelous Designer, please be mindful that this compatibility will only be available from the new patch version and onward. Hope this is understandable, and please contact us at support@marvelousdesigner.com for any other questions you may have.

post_details: I'm using cinema4D to create the UV, then iI export to MD via OBJ. this is how it looks on C4D Why in MD is so different? Sometimes, with complex shapes it fails to trace 2d patterns, is there any specific roules to follow?
post_description: This webpage aims to explore the discrepancies in 2D tracing of UV maps between Cinema 4D and Marvelous Designer, addressing common issues and best practices for effective pattern tracing.

comments.comment_body: Hi Monlinari. Thank you for contacting us, The "Trace 2D Patterns from UV Map" feature would not work with circular UVs because the pattern pieces in Marvelous Designer need at least one segment point to function, and for a circle, the software can not find a place to create a segment point. When using the "Trace 2D Patterns from UV Map" feature, you still need to follow the basic pattern-making principles when laying out your UVs. The below image is what a pattern for a sphere would look like in pattern making. Best regards, Marvelous Designer Support Team
Thank you
Hi 903135353343 still some problems with C4D, this is what MD gets from C4D UV What can I do to get all the parts?

Hi Monlinari, It seems like the only UV shell that was not able to be traced by the "Trace 2D Patterns from UV Map" feature is the circular piece. The "Trace 2D Patterns from UV Map" feature would not work with circular UVs because the pattern pieces in Marvelous Designer need at least one segment point to function, and for a circle, the software can not find a place to create a segment point. However, you can simply cut your circle UV in half, and in Marvelous Designer, you can chose to stitch it together or merge the lines to get your circle pattern back. Or create the circle using the create circle tool in Marvelous Designer using the measurement of your circle in C4D. You can single left click with the circle tool selected and input the Diameter, Radius or Circumference value to create your circle. Best regards, Marvelous Designer Support Team

post_title: How can I make garments collide with trim?
post_details: I would like to make all pieces of my garment collide with an obj that I imported as a trim. Is that possible? There is a "Collider" checkbox in the property editor, however, it is greyed out and can't be activated.
post_description: This web page aims to provide guidance on enabling garment collision with imported trim objects in 3D design software.

comments.comment_body: I too have had issues with this. I would like to know what the answer is.

Here is a link to the manual https://marvelousdesigner.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4406632098969-OBJ-Trim-Properties To have Trim collision: toggle on or off it MUST NOT be attached to anything. then you can attach it after you have turned it on or off. We are working on improving the feature and know a few existing bugs but follow the information in the manual and you can use that option with trims to "unglue" from the garment to toggle this option: right click the trim and choose "UNGLUE" to bring back that dialogue box.
So it is not possible to have a dangling solid rigid pieces collide with the cloth? How can one make something solid/rigid (i.e. medallion or jewelry) that can collide with the cloth?

903974176863 read the manual I linked above. It is possible in V11 +, you must glue the imported trim AFTER you have turned on collision. This only works with files that are imported AS a "trim" type in the import options. no matter what you do it MUST be "glued" to one garment. I do not know if you could say, do a string of curtain rings that hold eachother up like a daisy chain, you would have to test that.
This workflow is silly. I do hope it gets fixed soon. Okay. I'll give it a shot. Thanks.

Hi, thanks for the reply. The documentation you pointed to states that the collider checkbox "only enables or disables the Collision of detached trim." So, am I right to assume that glued trims cannot collide?

6069176090905 glued trim CAN collide only IF collission is toggled ON before you glue it. Think of it as you are stuck with your choice of "yes or no" collission once you glue it on ("unglue" removes the trim from the piece and turns on the toggle option again, but it moves in 3D space so your positioning is lost). I hope that makes more sense.
Can you create an example vidcap or something because I have found that it does not work in the non-gpu solvers.

Unfortunately, There is a bug that the collision is missing when its "glued" but collision works when its not glued. Which is why it is not working for you. Thank you for sharing so that we were able to find the bug, I will report it to the team.
Ok, I'm glad we found the issue :) When can we expect a fix to this? Is there any temporary workaround?

I have made a flat layered version of my 3d trim object (think rectangular medallion on a necklace) and made a few copies above and below to give it volume. I tweaked each layer until it kinda matched the overall object volume but as slices. I sewed the pieces together at the edges then selected the faces with the lasso select, right-clicked and selected solidify. I made the fabric Leather to keep it stiffer. This created a sort of layered cake version of a rigid object. It is tedious, but it works okay.
Unfortunately, that is not a viable solution in my case due to the complexity of the trim's geometry. When can we expect a fix?
Hi again, I would really like to use this feature in one of my projects, would you be so kind as to let us know when we can expect a fix?
Unfortunately, I do not have a timeline to provide you we submitted the bug that same day and we know that the dev team is on it. Other than that, even I have no other information at this time.

Hopefully the MD team can make a proper solution for this, but until then try this workaround. Instead of using trims, you can import OBJs as avatars, and set the skin offset to zero. The Avatar will not simulate obviously, but it works well for things such as buckles.

I am having the same problem with something that should be so simple, namely my character just having a belt buckle and a belt. There just doesn't seem to be a way of solving it with MD so that it simulates and folds the clothing underneath correctly. It is really frustrating. I actually stopped my MD subscription last year to look at other tools to simulate cloth including Blender and Houdini.
This bug seems to not be fixed yet, is there a workaround or anything new :)?

No!!! It is really annoying. I have been trying to combine the clothes animation with blender and houdini to try and make something work. No idea when Marvellous are going to fix this bug... if ever. Have been working on an Unreal project using Realallusion characters and really struggling with custom clothing.

11136053397529 For complete solids you 100% have to use another software but I managed to import fbx as a garment and apply a material with the trim_leather... preset. Collisions are again not perfect but may work in some cases. I really hope this bug gets fixed.
Having the same problem with the default trims that come with marvelous designer. Did this ever get fixed?
2024 and still unable to make a simple belt or buckle or anchor any hard surface object to clothing :( I really hope this will ever get fixed, it's a huge detriment to many projects in MD.
